goalInOwnWords: Build a line of machines that turns scrap into things that sell, fill each shift's order, and beat Sal's total money.
stoppedWhere: Today's yard, retry from shift 5, with the forecast saying $50 short of the order and a spare Splitter on the shelf; I went to Menu, Save and go home, then the survey.
stoppedWhy: I had finished the three lessons and one whole game and was told I was $50 short again, with Sal repeating that the furnace was the slow one. I could not tell what to do about it, and I was afraid of pressing the wrong thing and spoiling it, so I stopped rather than fiddle.

stuck.where: Lesson 2, shift 2, placing the second Hopper's belt
stuck.what: The conveyor on the shelf was already glowing, I tapped the lit spot and nothing happened, and I did not know why.
stuck.gotOutHow: Tapped the conveyor on the shelf again, then the spot.

stuck.where: Today's yard, shift 5 (and again on the retry)
stuck.what: The forecast said $50 short of the order and Sal said the Furnace was the slow one, but I could not see what to change. The spare Splitter only offered 'Sell Splitter'.
stuck.gotOutHow: Did not get out. I sold the spare parts for $10 each, which did not change the forecast, started the shift, missed the order by $50, then stopped on the retry.

confused: Lesson 1, shift 1: the sign said 'Line closed' and 'Start the shift' while the Crusher and Furnace boxes were still not ticked.
The goal said 'Ship 20 ingots' but shift 1 and 2 only made scrap and shards, with 0 ingots.
A spare Crusher sat on the shelf in lesson 2 and I did not know whether to use it.
Selling spare parts: I was not sure the Sell buttons would not sell something I needed.
The job card on today's yard has many new words at once: orders, raise, truck, Sal's game.
'$50 short of the order' while the 'sell for $10' buttons do not change what the shift pays.
What the red dot on the order row meant until I read the shift summary.
annoyed: The bottom part of the screen shows ghost text from the next card over the buttons during changes, which is hard to read.
Needing to tap the shelf piece again when it already looked picked.
Missing an order by only $50 after being warned and not being given a way to fix it.
Sal repeating 'the Furnace is the slow one' even after I added a Tuner.
pleased: Sal tells me the next step in plain words each time, like a patient teacher.
The lessons were short and I felt clever by the end of the first.
'This shift will pay $X' before I start is wonderful.
Shift by shift against Sal at the end, and the sentence about which card he used.
The 'What held you back' notes after each shift.
bestMoment: Lesson 1, shift 3: placing the Furnace and watching ingots take me from $111 to $576 with all three stars.
worstMoment: Being told I was $50 short, not knowing what to do, and doing it again on the retry.
oneChange: When the forecast says how short I am, tell me the one move that closes the gap, or what the spare part is for, in plain words.
